Q: Weird backticks behaviour in Active Record in CodeIgniter 2.0.3 A:

Use this line before your query:

$this->db->_protect_identifiers=false;

This will stop adding backticks to the built query.

Q: How to add an ORDER BY clause using CodeIgniter's query builder A:
  • A from() call is not needed if the table name is declared in the get() call.
  • The default sorting direction in SQL is "ascending"; it is not necessary to explicitly state 'asc' as the direction when using CodeIgniter's order_by().
  • The signature of order_by() is:
    public function order_by($orderby, $direction = '', $escape = NULL)
    • $orderby only expects a string type value; do not pass in an array of expressions.
    • $direction will only respect (case-insensitively) asc and desc.
    • Any value passed as $escape that is not a boolean will fallback to the _protect_identifiers setting. The only reason to ever pass a true value as $escape would be if _protect_identifiers is set to false - which is atypical.
    • Multiple rules can be expressed in a single order_by() call by delimiting with commas in the $orderby parameter. For example: name, id DESC or name DESC, id or name, id or name DESC, id DESC 
      $this->db->order_by('name, category, id', 'desc');
// ORDER BY `name` DESC, `category` DESC, `id` DESC
    • Multiple rules can be expressed via multiple order_by() calls - the order of these calls will be respected in the rendered SQL.
      $this->db->order_by('name', 'desc')->order_by('id');
// ORDER BY `name` DESC, `id`
    • From CodeIgniter 3, order_by() will implicitly disable escaping on expressions which include a single-quote or parenthesis. This means that in such cases, it is not necessary to explicitly pass a false third parameter. 
      $this->db->order_by("COALESCE(id, 0)")
// ORDER BY COALESCE(id, 0)
  • Query builder method calls can be made in any order so long as they are called before the "executing" method call (e.g. get(), get_where(), get_compiled_select(), update(), insert() to name a few).
  • Chain your query builder methods together for maximum elegance. Even chain the result set generator to the query executing method.
  • It is not necessary to explicitly call select() to build a SELECT clause if the intention is to fetch all columns. CodeIgniter will add SELECT * by default when omitted.
public function getAllSortedByNameAsc(): array
{
    return $this->db->order_by('name')->get($this->table_name)->result();
}

This model method will return an array of zero or more objects.

CodeIgniter will render and execute the following SQL (assuming $this->table_name = 'foo'):

SELECT *
FROM `foo`
ORDER BY `name`

Q: Is there a kind of udev equivalent on Windows? A:

Thanks to Ben Voigt, who points out that there are command line tools to configure devices devcon seems to allow device management and pnputil seems to manage device drivers.

As far as I know, the only way to configure devices in Windows is via the device management UI which can be started with mmc devmgmt.msc

This is obviously not even similar or even close to udev, there isn’t any possibility to do this without the GUI.

Q: How do you translate this regular-expression idiom from Perl into Python? A:

Another way of using := with any which I think is clearer than the original Perl:

import re

s = 'bob dob barhop'

patterns = {r'foo(.+)', r'bar(.+)', r'baz(.+)'}
    
if any(m:=re.search(p, s) for p in patterns):
    print(f"pattern r'{m.re.pattern}' captures '{m.group(1)}'")
else:
    print('no match')

Prints:

pattern r'bar(.+)' captures 'hop'

Q: How can I install Python 3.11 in windows for Tensorflow A:

Just follow the most evident way:

  • navigate to the official Python site: http://python.org
  • then follow the Downloads link
  • then follow the Python for Windows link

On that page you will find installers for versions from 3.11.0 to 3.11.9 for whatever environment you need (32 bits, 64 bits or ARM64).

Any of those installers allow either a for all users installation which does require administrative privileges or a for you only one which does not.
